 Toyota Recalls 62,000 Tundras Over Camshaft Failure
 Off-Road.com Follow Chris Thu, November 19, 2026 at 10:30 AM UTC Add to Preferred Sources Thu, November 19, 2026 at 10:30 AM UTC Toyota has issued a safety recall covering roughly 62,000 Tundra pickups because a defective engine camshaft can fracture during driving. The defect applies to certain nonhybrid 2022-2023 and 2025-2026 Tundra models.
 What's Wrong
 A supplier reportedly built some camshafts incorrectly. If one breaks while the truck is moving, the engine can lose motive power, which Toyota says is especially dangerous at highway speeds. For anyone who runs a Tundra out on remote dirt roads or deep into the backcountry, a sudden loss of power is the kind of failure you want sorted before you leave pavement. Toyota estimates that roughly 300 bad camshafts actually left the line. The problem is that the company cannot pin down which trucks received them, so it has to inspect roughly 62,000 vehicles to find the small batch of bad parts.
 The Fix
 Dealers will check the camshaft on each recalled truck. If a technician finds the part traces back to the flawed production lot, the dealer swaps it at no cost. Because this targets a specific manufacturing lot, most owners who bring their trucks in will likely pass inspection and head home with the original camshaft intact.
 Not the First Tundra Engine Issue
 This recall is separate from the larger run of Tundra engine problems that have followed the current-generation truck since launch. In 2024, more than 100,000 Tundra pickups and Lexus LX SUVs got new engines after debris left behind during manufacturing raised the risk of V6 engine failure. The camshaft recall is unrelated to that earlier campaign.
 Check Your VIN
 Automakers try to notify every affected owner, but they don't always reach everyone, and a truck can be subject to more than one recall over its life. Owners can confirm whether their Tundra is included by looking it up with a VIN, license plate, or the vehicle's year, make, and model through a recall lookup tool. If you wheel or overland in one of these trucks, running your VIN now is worth the few minutes it takes.
